subject: Linguistics
title: The Regularity Hypothesis
description: A quick win: understand The Regularity Hypothesis.

hook.text: If p became f in one word, it became f in all words—no exceptions. That's the bold claim.

buildup.text: The Neogrammarians in the 1870s declared: sound laws operate without exception.

discovery.text: Apparent exceptions are explained by competing rules, borrowing, or analogy—not by randomness.

twist.text: This hypothesis was controversial—but it made historical linguistics genuinely scientific.

climax.text: Regularity allows reconstruction: if you know the rules, you can work backward to the ancestor.

punchline.text: Sound change plays by rules—and the rules never cheat.
